subject: general
question: Which of the following can be applied as a goodness-of-fit test?
solution:
The correct answer is** Χ2 test**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Χ2** test:**

 
 
• The Χ2 test (Chi-square test) is a statistical method used to determine if there is a significant difference between the expected and observed frequencies in categorical data.
 
• In the context of a financial enterprise, the Χ2 test can be applied to assess the goodness-of-fit for models predicting financial behaviors, such as customer defaults, credit risks, or market trends.
 
• It helps in validating whether the observed data fits a particular distribution, which is crucial for making informed financial decisions and risk assessments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **t-test:**

 
 
• The t-test is used to compare the means of two groups and determine if they are significantly different from each other. It is not typically used for goodness-of-fit tests but rather for hypothesis testing regarding population means.
 
 
 
• **F-test:**
 
 
• The F-test is used to compare two variances and to test the hypothesis that the variances of two populations are equal. It is not used for goodness-of-fit testing but for comparing models and regression analysis.
 
 
 
• **Z-test:**
 
 
• The Z-test is used to determine whether there is a significant difference between sample and population means or between the means of two samples, especially when the sample size is large. It is not designed for goodness-of-fit testing.
